    Fundamental Rights (Articles 13-32)

            Article          Provision

                         Government cannot make laws that take away basic rights; any old law against these
            Article 13

            Article 14       Everyone is treated equally by law and gets equal protection, no matter who they are.

                         Government cannot treat people unfairly based on religion, caste, gender, race, or place
            Article 15

            Article 16       Everyone gets a fair chance to apply for government jobs without unfair discrimination.

                             Untouchability is banned, and treating someone as inferior because of caste is a
            Article 17
                            punishable offence.

                         Government cannot give titles like “Raja” or “Sir,” except for education or military
            Article 18
                           achievements.

                          People can speak freely, meet peacefully, form groups, move anywhere, live anywhere,
            Article 19

                     No one can be punished for past actions, punished twice for same crime, or forced to
            Article 20

                     On Life and Liberty: No one can be deprived of life or freedom unless proper legal
            Article 21
                          procedure is followed.

            Article 21A      Every child between 6 to 14 years must get free and compulsory education.

                            Arrested person must be told reasons, get a lawyer, and be taken to a judge within 24
            Article 22
                             hours.

            Article 24        Children below 14 years cannot work in factories, mines, or dangerous jobs.

            Article 32       People can go to the Supreme Court if their basic rights are violated.

     Article 32 & 226

             Article 32: If your fundamental rights are violated, you can directly go to Supreme Court for
              justice and protection. This article gives the Supreme Court power to issue writs to protect

Fundamental Rights.

             Habeas Corpus: Court orders that a detained person must be brought before it to check
                          if the detention is legal.

             Mandamus: Court orders a public officer to do their duty if they refuse or fail to perform
                   their legal responsibility.

                  Prohibition: Higher court stops a lower court from continuing a case when it is acting
              beyond its legal powers.

                   Certiorari: Higher court cancels the decision of a lower court if it acted beyond powers
                 or violated fair rules.

            Quo Warranto: Court asks a person to show authority for holding a public post and
              removes them if they are not eligible.

             Article 226: High Courts can give orders (writs) to protect our rights and solve problems,
            not just fundamental rights but other legal rights too.

     State Legislature

           Vidhan Sabha (Lower House of Legislative Assembly):

                This is the main law-making house in a state legislative assembly where people elect
             members to make laws for them. All states have it. States with only this one house are
                 called single-house states or states with Unicameral Legislature.

             Members are elected for 5 years, but the Governor can dissolve a Vidhan Sabha earlier
                          if needed under Article 174(2)(b).

           Vidhan Parishad (Upper House of Legislative Assembly):

It is a permanent house, so it never ends. Every 2 years, some members leave and new
              ones join.

                      Its size is limited—it cannot be more than one-third of Vidhan Sabha or 40 members,
               whichever is greater as per Article 171.

                         If a state wants it, Parliament can create or remove it under Article 169.

              These 6 states have two houses—Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka,
              Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana.
